title: Enrollment reconciler
hints: Write two tiny normalisers first, _serial(v) -> (v or "").strip().upper() and _user(v) -> (v or "").strip().lower(), and use them everywhere a serial or user is read. That single habit removes half of the messy-data bugs.
index_by_serial is one loop: skip empty serials, add to the duplicates set when the serial is already in the dict, otherwise store the row. Do not overwrite: the spec says the first row wins.

Write decide as a ladder of guard clauses in exactly the numbered order of the spec, each returning a tuple. Rules 3 and 4 return None when the device is not in mdm, so compute `mdm_row is not None` and reuse it.

In reconcile iterate over set(mdm_by) | set(inv_by), look each serial up in both dicts with .get, work out duplicate_in from the two duplicate sets (mdm first), and sort the final list with key=lambda a: (a["action"], a["serial"]).
